cards.title: Give this project a way to reach Hugging Face and a GPU
cards.plain: Nobody can download the model weights with the project's tool yet. Their hashes must be recorded first, and that needs huggingface.co, which the agent pod cannot reach.
cards.why: `tools/download_weights.py` refuses any repo without a pinned commit and SHA-256, and every pin in `tools/weights.lock.json` is still empty (#2). The same egress gap stops locking the real TensorRT wheels from pypi.nvidia.com (#3) and any GPU test of 0.1.0 (#4). I asked build-office on the forum for pod egress or a Spark task runner; this card is for the part only you can approve.
steps: Open the forum topic https://build.chappa.ai/forum?t=912562b42157e511966d9099 ("Pod egress for huggingface.co and pypi.nvidia.com").
Approve egress for pod-personalive-blackwell to `huggingface.co` (plus the download hosts it redirects to) and `pypi.nvidia.com`, or a GPU task route to sparky, whichever build-office proposes.
cards.verify: Next session I run `python tools/download_weights.py --pin`, and `tools/weights.lock.json` gets real hashes (#2 closes).
cards.blocks: #2 weight pins, #3 TensorRT lock, #4 GPU validation

cards.title: No Go rewrite: stays Python
cards.plain: The project stays in Python, because its core (PyTorch, TensorRT, diffusers) has no Go equivalent; the security problems were outdated dependencies, now fixed.
cards.chosen: Python with a full hash lock (`requirements.txt`, made by `tools/lock.sh`), Dependabot on, dep-audit in the office. A local dep-audit of 0.1.0 found 0 advisories in 90 dependencies.

cards.title: The webcam page is a local tool, not an admin dashboard
cards.plain: The webcam page runs on your own machine, like a desktop app. So it gets no security self-check page and no BUILD link; the server itself is locked down instead.
cards.why: The self-check and BUILD-link rules cover web admin dashboards. This page has no accounts, settings or admin, only one live animation session.
cards.chosen: Server hardening, described in `SECURITY.md`: access key, 127.0.0.1 by default, TLS needed for any other address, strict CSP and security headers, Origin check, one session at a time, size-checked image decode.
cards.if_ignored: Stays as is. Overturn this if you want the self-check page anyway.

cards.title: The webcam server always needs an access key
cards.plain: The webcam server works only for people with its access key. It listens on this machine only by default, and any other address must use TLS.
cards.chosen: `--host` defaults to 127.0.0.1; any other host needs `--ssl-certfile` and `--ssl-keyfile`. The key comes from a mode-600 file (`--access-key-file` or `PERSONALIVE_ACCESS_KEY_FILE`, at least 32 characters); without one, a new key is made for each run and printed with the address. No key in env, code or compose.

about.what: A fork of GVCLab's PersonaLive (real-time live portrait animation from a webcam and one reference photo), made to run on NVIDIA Blackwell: DGX Spark GB10 and mixed RTX GPUs.
about.why: Upstream PersonaLive does not run as-is on GB10 (sm_121) and pulled in many known-vulnerable dependencies; this fork runs on current torch and TensorRT and is kept free of known vulnerabilities, with no npm.
about.who: The owner, and anyone with an NVIDIA GPU who wants live portrait animation (the repo is public).
